## About this page

*Only in the desktop app.*

How WM Pass behaves on this computer: the tray, starting when you sign in, quick search from anywhere, and auto-type.

#### How it works

**Window** decides what closing and starting do. **From anywhere** sets the keys that open quick search over other programs. **Typing for you** lets quick search type a login for you.

See also [Quick search window](/guide/screens/#screen-palette), [Typing logins with auto-type](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-autotype), [Browser extension](/guide/settings/browser/), [SSH agent](/guide/settings/ssh/).

<a id="setting-close-to-tray"></a>

## Keep running in the tray

*Only in the desktop app.*

Closing the window leaves WM Pass running in the tray, where it still locks on time.

#### Why it is there

Scheduled backups, quick search, the browser extension link and the SSH agent all need WM Pass running. With this on, closing the window does not stop them.

#### How it works

Click the tray icon to bring the window back. Its menu also has **Quick Search**, **Lock** and **Quit WM Pass**.

#### Limits

With [Lock when the window is hidden](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-on-hide) also on, closing the window locks the vault, so quick search, auto-type, the extension and the SSH agent have nothing to offer until you unlock again.

See also [Start hidden](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-start-hidden), [Lock when the window is hidden](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-on-hide), [How often](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-schedule).

<a id="setting-start-hidden"></a>

## Start hidden

*Only in the desktop app.*

WM Pass starts in the tray, with no window, until you open it.

#### When to use it

With [Open when you sign in](/guide/settings/desktop/#action-autostart), so WM Pass is ready for quick search and the extension without a window in the way.

See also [Open when you sign in](/guide/settings/desktop/#action-autostart), [Keep running in the tray](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-close-to-tray).

<a id="action-autostart"></a>

## Open when you sign in

*Only in the desktop app.*

Starts WM Pass when you sign in to this computer.

#### How it works

The system keeps this choice, not WM Pass, so a settings file does not carry it. On macOS it is a launch agent.

#### When to use it

Turn on [Start hidden](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-start-hidden) as well to have it wait in the tray. Scheduled backups then run without you opening the app.

See also [Start hidden](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-start-hidden), [Keep running in the tray](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-close-to-tray).

<a id="setting-global-palette"></a>

## Quick search

*Only in the desktop app.*

The keys that open a small search box over whatever you are doing, from any program.

#### How it works

Click the row and press the keys you want. **No shortcut** turns it off.

In quick search, Enter copies the password, or the code for an item that has only a code. Ctrl+Enter, or Command+Enter on a Mac, copies the username. With [Auto-type](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-auto-type-enabled) on, Shift+Enter types the login.

The box closes when you click away from it.

#### Limits

If another program already uses those keys, WM Pass says so and does not take them. Choose others.

See also [Quick search window](/guide/screens/#screen-palette), [Auto-type](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-auto-type-enabled), [Clear the clipboard after](/guide/settings/security/#setting-clipboard-seconds).

<a id="setting-auto-type-enabled"></a>

## Auto-type

*Only in the desktop app.*

Lets quick search type a login into the program behind WM Pass, so the password never goes on the clipboard.

<figure class="guide-figure">
<div class="guide-frame">
<div class="guide-row"><div class="guide-box"><strong>Quick search</strong><span>Shift+Enter on a login</span></div></div>
<div class="guide-down">↓</div>
<div class="guide-row"><div class="guide-box warn"><strong>System input</strong><span>other programs can see it</span></div></div>
<div class="guide-down">↓</div>
<div class="guide-row"><div class="guide-box"><strong>The window in front</strong><span>username, Tab, password</span></div></div>
</div>
<figcaption>Auto-type presses the keys for you. Typed text passes through the system, where other programs can see it.</figcaption>
</figure>

#### How it works

Open quick search over a sign-in form, pick the item and press Shift+Enter. WM Pass hides, waits a moment for the other program to take the focus back, then types the username, Tab and the password. An item with no username gets the password alone.

It types into whatever has the focus at that moment, and does not press Enter.

#### When to use it

For sign-in windows the browser extension cannot reach, such as another desktop program's.

#### Limits

Typed text goes through the system's input queue, where other programs can see it.

macOS asks for Accessibility permission the first time. On Linux it works under X11; Wayland desktops usually refuse.

WM Pass cannot tell a sign-in form from a chat box. Check which window is in front before you press Shift+Enter.

See also [Typing logins with auto-type](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-autotype), [Quick search](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-global-palette), [Clear the clipboard after](/guide/settings/security/#setting-clipboard-seconds).
